expectation: Membrane rings on helper/regulatory T cells, which are common in a tumour and form dense aggregates or stromal bands among tumour nests. Monocytes and macrophages stain dim. Stained cells should overlap CD3+ cells and leave tumour nests negative.
observed: A: strong, uneven staining in stromal and immune-rich regions, varying between images, with tumour nests dark. B and C: sparse, few cells. D: yellow membrane outlines around blue nuclei. E: CD4 sits closely on the CD3-dense regions, white in the merge, and CD3-negative areas are dark.
why: The CD4 stain is membranous, lies in immune-rich stroma and overlaps CD3+ T-cell areas, so the population is clear and specific.
notes: CD4 outlines cells as membrane rings in lymphoid-rich stromal regions and largely overlaps CD3 in row E, while tumour nests and CD3-negative areas stay dark. This is a real stain.
